text:
Devon Levi has given Edmonton what any coach in his first season wants from a goalie: wins. The former Sabre is 10-3-0 in 13 starts under Mike Babcock, and CBS Sports had him cruising to win No. 10. Daily Faceoff Edmonton's Oilersnation asked the obvious question: "What has Devon Levi done to get this team to love and embrace him so much?"

The honest answer from our numbers is that he has been solid and the team has done the rest. He has allowed 37 goals on 37.4 expected (what his shots against usually produce), right on average, with an .891 save percentage. He's better than the league on low-danger shots (.974 against .962), about level on high-danger ones (.681 against .684), and 13.5% of his saves lead to another shot within three seconds (league 10.7%). That rebound rate is the weak spot.

His last ten starts have swung: a shutout in Toronto on Nov. 14, then seven goals allowed in Carolina on Nov. 21. For a 212th overall pick with a .952 season at Northeastern, starting and winning in the NHL is already a story. Watch the rebounds.
